source_first_claims.claim: Visual singleton search operationally uses exogenous attentional allocation; top-down selective factors must be controlled.
V1 hypothesis: local salience equals relative maximum V1 neural population response at each location, regardless of the winning neuron feature tuning.
Iso-feature contextual suppression releases response of appropriately tuned neurons at singleton compared with identically featured background bars.
The target is a parameter-free distributional behavioral test, NOT fully parameterized V1 network simulation or neuronal recording.
For fixed background other-item response distribution, higher maximum V1 target response yields monotonically shorter salience-driven singleton-search RT under fixed motor/readout mapping.
Each singleton’s response distribution is treated as statistically independent of the fixed non-target background and appropriate other feature fluctuations.
For C/O/CO example, absence of CO jointly tuned neuron yields response-to-RT minimum-race equality, motivating model controls.
Feature-specific V1 neural response maxima distinguish alternative color-tuned, orientation-tuned and joint-tuned cell contributions.
Source expands conditions to seven singleton categories C,M,O,CM,CO,MO,CMO on matched homogeneous color/motion/orientation backgrounds.
The derivation uses RT induced by a monotone transform of maximum evoked V1 population responses, and race minima correspond to maximum of response collections.
Jointly feature-tuned CO and MO cells yield expected violations of some simple double- and triple-feature spurious race equalities.
CM jointly tuned cell prevalence and response strength is uncertain in original source, making relevant spurious equality ambiguous.
Original central non-spurious race equality: min(RT_CMO, RT_C, RT_M, RT_O) =d min(RT_CM, RT_CO, RT_MO) assuming no V1 CMO-tuned cells.

source_first_claims.original_source_locator: p16 Eq30 and p32–34 Methods Eq39
source_first_claims.claim: Eq30 is derived via identical maxima over six classes of V1 neurons C/M/O/CM/CO/MO on both sides of the response-to-RT mapping.
The CMO RT distribution is indirectly predicted by distributional data from six other singleton conditions of the SAME observer, no fitted free prediction parameters.
The source Fig6 shows example observer SA p=.094; Fig7 shows all six observers’ Eq30 predictions non-rejected at p>.05, NOT independently reproduced statistics.
Matched-complexity spurious control equalities RE6 and RE7 are falsified for illustrated subject SA, whereas RE8 is not.
Source reports 80 or 320 analysis configurations across bin counts, bin definitions and discrepancy metrics; RE1 robustness limited by empirical statistical power.
In green vs purple trials rapid color pop-out creates potential latency floor and weaker rejection of some spurious controls.
Previously collected Koene/Zhaoping 2007 RT data used: 30x22 bar grid; 18 possible target cells, left/right manual press, seven singleton categories.
About 300 RT per singleton type per observer split into green/purple pools averaging ~150 each; eight original observers but only six recorded CMO.
Excluded incorrect presses, RT<.2s and subject/category RT>3 SD; reused stimulus/calibration means findings are task-conditioned.
Non-spurious Eq30 proof hinges on feature-matched distribution invariances and max/min race identity; not proof across alternative sensorimotor distributions.
Original conditional interpretation suggests extrastriate weak salience contribution for these singleton scenes only if extrastriate triple-tuned responses materially break Eq30.
Original explicit alternative: extrastriate CMO responses can be negligible or satisfy Eq35, preserving behavioral Eq30 even with extrastriate participation.
Original authors flag independent fluctuations, fixed background, non-tuned-feature invariance, contrast normalization, imperfect isoluminance and stable perceptual learning as idealizations.
Complex images, multiple eye movements, goal-driven predictable feature attention violate simple RT monotonicity; no full cognitive generative model identified.
The V1 race model descends from early Li/Zhaoping V1 saliency work and reutilizes original Koene/Zhaoping 2007 behavioral trial data, not wholly novel invented mechanism.
